FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Contact: Betsy Russell 208-336-2854, president@cabi-boise.org Cue the corned beef, pickles and pastrami: Deli Days is back! Deli Days, Idaho’s Jewish Festival, returns to Boise this summer, on Sunday, August 23r d, from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Congregation Ahavath Beth Israel (CABI), 11 N. Latah St. in Boise. Experience Jewish food, music and culture at this longstanding Treasure Valley festival, which first was held 40 years ago in 1986, when the historic synagogue was located on State Street, prior to its 2003 move to the Bench. Deli Days is CABI’s largest community event of the year, involving dozens of volunteers from the congregation. This beloved, longstanding community tradition went on hiatus for a number of years, through COVID, and returned in 2024 rebranded as the Idaho Jewish Festival. This year, the full Deli Days is back on. That means congregants at the oldest continuously operating synagogue west of the Mississippi have been baking and preparing for months, and we’ll welcome our larger community for the festival with kosher-style pastrami, corned beef, hot dogs, pickles, lox and bagels, knishes, a wide array of Jewish baked goods, beer, wine, soda, live music and dancing, kids’ activities, tours of our historic synagogue and more. Plans are under way to manage crowds and minimize lines. But we can’t promise that we won’t run out of some items before the festival closes at 7 p.m., so come early for the best selection. We do promise entertainment, drinks, synagogue tours and noshes will last until closing; put it on your calendar, and plan to join us for the fun! #####
